newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba blames people from U.S. for hotel explosions.
newsitem.headline: Cuba blames people from U.S. for hotel explosions.

text.p: Cuba's Interior Ministry said on Saturday it had evidence that the people responsible for exploding two devices in two Havana hotels earlier in the day were from the United States.
"The Interior Ministry has evidence that the people responsible for these deeds and also the materials they used came from the United States," said a brief ministry statement read on state radio.
The statement said the explosions that rocked the lobbies of the Hotel Nacional and the Hotel Capri around 11.35 a.m. local time (1535 GMT) were caused by "explosive artifacts."
It said they slightly wounded three people and caused damage to windows and furniture in the two hotels.
The statement did not give any further information. It did it say if anyone had been arrested in connection with the explosions.

The Nacional and Capri hotels are around 200 yards (metres) apart in Havana's central Vedado district. Reporters were not allowed to enter the hotels after the explosions but the damage to the ground floor of the Capri was clearly visible from the street.
